text:
Josh Morrissey played 9.5 minutes against Colorado on October 7 and didn't dress again until November 10. Since coming back he has been back at about 24 minutes a night, with a 32.8-minute marathon in Chicago, and the Jets have won eight of the ten games in his log. His first goal of the season was an overtime winner over the Islanders, and he carries a four-game point streak into the weekend.

The points (9 in 12 games) run a little ahead of the play. At five on five the Jets have had 46.9% of the expected goals, our measure of chance quality, with him on the ice, and his teammates have scored about 12 more goals than those chances usually produce. That cushion tends to thin out. What doesn't is the passing: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 6.0 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 86th percentile among defensemen, and Evolving-Hockey ranked him 17th of 215 defensemen at 2.5 wins above replacement. Our numbers project 48 points.
headline: Morrissey is back, and the Jets haven't lost much since
